cardinality_bindings.alternative_reading: An alternative reading could treat this as concurrent_regions cardinality (three orthogonal regions PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion under PumpControl) since the closed model and canonical IR do implement each substate inside its own composite region; NL2 itself, however, names states rather than regions, so explicit_named_members remains primary while concurrent_regions is preserved here as a competent alternative for D review.
cardinality_bindings.basis: NL2 text ('Within the PumpControl state, there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState.'); exact_source_inventory states PumpControl (source_id PumpControl) and its descendants PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion each containing one of PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState; closed_model_inventory/inspection_equivalent_facts.states row for PumpControl at state:PumpControl:line:2.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL2 explicitly enumerates three named substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) as the members owned by PumpControl; this is a finite named-member enumeration, not a region-structure or generic direct-child-state count, so explicit_named_members is the primary domain. The owner is PumpControl, matching the contract's scope_concept, and its owned closed-model ref is state:PumpControl:line:2.

result.reason: The closed FCSTM shows PumpControl entering only a synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf state with no outgoing transitions, while PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion and their PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState children are all structurally unreachable_from_initial per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts. This breaks the owner-local initial entry from PumpControl into PumpState (NL3), and consequently makes the required PumpState->WaterState and WaterState->MethaneState transitions (NL4/NL5) unreachable from root even though the edges exist in the finite transition inventory. It also leaves the state-owned actions in PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState (NL3-ACTION-1 and derived NL4/NL5 action contracts) unreachable operationally. I derive one additional reachability contract at the PumpControl-owned PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion scope because NL's sequential substate chain (NL3-NL5) requires these substates to actually be enterable, which is a distinct property from the local edge (PumpRegion.[*]->PumpState) existing structurally but being unreachable from root. I keep the NL3-INITIAL-1 owner-entry candidate separate (PumpControl has no edge to PumpState/PumpRegion, only to UnspecifiedInitial) and keep the deadlock/frontier fact (UnspecifiedInitial leaf) as V1 evidence for the same owner-entry defect rather than manufacturing a new deadlock contract, since UnspecifiedInitial is a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder not an author-specified operating state.

stage_receipts.reason: NL1 establishes root initial entry into PumpControl and introduces (context-only) that PumpControl can transition to substates based on conditions, without naming an exact source/target relation yet. NL2 establishes containment of three named substates within PumpControl. NL3 establishes owner-local initial entry from PumpControl into PumpState (first transition), plus a state-owned action obligation (pump activated/controlled) - treated as state_action since NL3 says "the pump is activated or controlled" which describes ongoing behavior in that substate. NL4 and NL5 continue the sequential narrative: "can also transition to WaterState" and "similarly...can transition to MethaneState" are read as continuing endpoints PumpState->WaterState and WaterState->MethaneState per the sequential-discourse rule (source continues from preceding target absent explicit reset), each with their own descriptive but non-progress state role (monitoring described, not an explicit continuous/repeated obligation beyond mention). I treat these as one shared-source group only where the discourse continues; however per rules, "can also transition" and "similarly can transition" without explicit alternative framing ("either/or") continue narrative order rather than forming alternatives from PumpState. Applying the sequential-discourse default: PumpControl-initial->PumpState, PumpState->WaterState, WaterState->MethaneState. Guard/condition qualifiers ("based on specific conditions") are preserved as context on NL1, not a separate guard contract since no exact condition is stated. Containment for all three substates under PumpControl is preserved regardless of transition source.
